title: What Do You Understand When Someone Says, "Python is an Interpreted Language"?

blocks.content: What Do You Understand When Someone Says, "Python is an Interpreted Language"?
Python is an interpreted language. Interpreted languages are executed line by line, unlike compiled languages, where the whole program is executed at once.
This means that even if there is an error in line 32, we will execute the code successfully till line 31.
In short, the Python interpreter executes instructions directly without compiling the entire program into machine language.
